  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Julie Lie, called the meeting to order at 4:34 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Lie

  Commissioners Absent: Hilliard, Wood

Also present: Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, Jennifer Santana, Community
Program Specialist.

Roll call taken by Jennifer Santana. Commissioner Wood was excused from the meeting and
Commissioner Hilliard was unexcused. Commissioner Chotiswatdi joined the meeting at 4:36 p.m.
and Commissioner Killion joined the meeting at 4:45 p.m.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  25-55319  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee meeting of Wednesday, August 6, 2025.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Bedy, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Noble, Russell, Scott, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Hilliard, Killion, Wood

2.  25-55322  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Mayor’s Fund and Policy
  Subcommittee and the Continuum of Care (CoC) Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee (HSAC) representative.

  Page 1 of 4

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Howat, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Wood

  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee
  • The subcommittee is currently working on the utility bill inserts scheduled for
  distribution in November and will be collaborating with City staff to help
  increase donations to the Mayor’s Fund.
  Policy Subcommittee
  • Chair Sarah Bedy reviewed the final draft of the Policy Recommendations
  and encouraged commissioners to meet with their respective Council
  representatives to discuss the proposed recommendations.
  • Commissioner Scott provided an update from her discussion at the CoC
  General Meeting, which included an announcement seeking service
  providers interested in supporting a pilot program that would offer portable
  showers and restrooms.
  CoC Updates
  • Commissioner Pat provided an update from the Long Beach CoC Board
  Retreat held on September 9, 2025. The Board received a presentation from
  LAHSA regarding the collaboration on the Homeless Management
  Information System (HMIS). There was also discussion about the NOFO
  renewal updates; however, no release date has been announced yet, as it
  remains pending due to the federal government shutdown.

3.  25-56577  Recommendation to approve the Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee grant application
  submitted by Priceless Investors for funding in the amount of $10,000.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Wood

  • The committee reviewed the application for Priceless Investors, which will

  one-page final summary required from all applicants prior to the release of
  the final payment.
  • The committee voted to approve the application for Priceless Investors in the
  amount of $10,000.

4.  25-54241  Recommendation to discuss and approve the meeting schedule for the Homeless
  Services Advisory Committee and subcommittees.

  A motion was made by Member Killion, seconded by Member Howat, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Scott, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 1  Russell
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Wood

  • The committee discussed maintaining the bi-monthly meeting schedule and
  requested that staff create a master calendar outlining the meeting dates,
  locations, and times to be shared with members.
  • Commissioner Doug made a friendly amendment to extend the Homeless
  Services Advisory Committee meetings to two hours. The meeting time will
  now be 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

5.  25-56537  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on Youth Homelessness from
  the health department.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 2  Hilliard, Wood

  • Bureau manager Paul Duncan provided the presentation on Youth
  Homelessness, the presentation included, the Homeless Count Overview,
  Insights from HMIS, and Youth Coordinated Entry in LA.
  • Chapin Hall provided the City with an initial report for consideration for the
  future work as well as consideration in the Long Beach Fiscal Year 2026.

  Page 3 of 4
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES

  • Long Beach has been working with Los Angeles Emissary to form policy
  recommendations and advocacy that is guided by youth. The City is
  expanding its youth-focused homeless services by adding new housing and
  prevention programs with dedicated funding. In addition, they are investing
  resources and strategically coordinating efforts including planning,
  partnerships, and funding initiatives to address and ultimately end youth
  homelessness in Long Beach.
  • Commissioners and staff discussed quality jobs and workforce readiness
  collaboration opportunities.

6.  25-55321  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff
  Operations and Updates Report from the Health Department.

  • This Agenda Item was laid over.

7.  25-55323  Recommendation to receive and file the future Homeless Services Advisory

  • This Agenda Item was laid over.

  • This was laid over.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • No public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • No announcemnets.

ADJOURNMENT

Chair Julie Lie adjourned the meeting at 6:05 p.m.
